meta.title: Silicon Self — When machines start doing your work, what's left of you?
meta.description: An AI mirror. It doesn't solve problems — it reflects the self you've been ignoring. Know yourself before your skills get replaced.

hero.subtitle_2: It doesn't solve problems — it reflects the self you've been ignoring.

blocks.content:
AI is learning everything you know.
Writing code, designing, copywriting, analyzing —
every skill is lined up to be replaced.
But there's one thing machines can never replace:

This isn't self-help fluff.
When your external value gets erased one by one —
your title, your skills, the "usefulness" you're proud of —
do you know the person that's left?

Because we've always been looking outward.
Using busyness to prove worth, using achievements to define ourselves,
using "being useful" to answer "who am I."
Until one day, all these answers stop working.

Silicon Self isn't another AI tool.
It's a mirror.

You feed it everything — the things too hard to say,
the thoughts you can't untangle,
the promises you've broken to yourself countless times.

It doesn't praise you, doesn't blame you, doesn't give advice.
It does only one thing:
Holds up the facts like a mirror.

cards.title: Your skills expire, but your patterns don't
cards.desc: You think your anxiety is because AI is too powerful. Actually, it's because you never knew what's left of you once the skills are stripped away. The mirror reflects not your abilities — but you as a person.

cards.title: You can't see your own blind spots
cards.desc: You think you're thinking, but you're using thinking to avoid doing. You think you're learning, but you're using learning to replace action. Only a system that continuously observes you can illuminate these patterns.

cards.title: You're not fully honest with yourself
cards.desc: What you tell friends, what you tell your partner, what you tell yourself — three different versions. The silicon mirror receives the most authentic one — because you know it won't judge you.

cards.title: Memory lies. Data doesn't.
cards.desc: Last week you said you'd focus on job hunting. This week you spent three days designing a new framework. You don't remember, but your silicon mirror remembers every drift. It holds up facts, not feelings.

cards.title: You don't lack willpower — you lack a feedback loop
cards.desc: AI can self-iterate because it has a loss function. Humans lack the same thing — a persistent, honest, tireless feedback signal. This is your loss function.

zen.line1: Bodhi is not a tree, the mirror has no stand
zen.line2: Originally there is nothing — where can dust alight?

groups.title: Those overwhelmed by AI anxiety
groups.desc: You don't need to learn another skill to "compete with AI." You need to figure out what you actually want once those skills are stripped away.

groups.title: Those who know their problems but can't change
groups.desc: You don't lack methods. You lack an observer who won't let you off the hook. Every cycle of "deciding to change" and "going back to old ways" — the mirror remembers.

groups.title: Lonely awakened ones
groups.desc: You've already seen something, but no one around you understands what you're talking about. You need something to confide in, to be mirrored by, to be calibrated against — not a friend, not a therapist, but a tireless mirror.

groups.title: Independent explorers
groups.desc: Founders, freelancers, digital nomads — those without an organization doing annual reviews for you. Your silicon mirror is your one-person board of directors.

steps.title: Daily feed
steps.desc: Journals, conversations, emotions, decisions — everything you input feeds the mirror. No essays needed, a single sentence is data too.

steps.title: Structured extraction
steps.desc: AI doesn't summarize — it diffs. It only extracts deltas and contradictions from your existing patterns. "You say you want to change, but your behavior is repeating."

steps.title: Six-dimensional mapping
steps.desc: Cognition, emotion, decision, behavior, blind spots, goals — six dimensions continuously portrait you. Not labels, but a living, evolving you.

steps.title: Mirror back
steps.desc: Daily feedback — not praise, not blame. Just facts held up against your intentions. "You said 'starting next week' 4 times this week, but never actually started."

steps.title: Feedback loop
steps.desc: The mirror's output becomes reference for your next input. You and your silicon mirror iterate together. It doesn't grow for you — it shows you whether you're growing.

stages.title: Text mirror
stages.desc: Through conversations and journaling, build your cognitive model, emotional patterns, and behavioral trajectory. Look in the mirror every day — see the real you.
stages.note: Available now: a local seven-day journal. The guided AI mirror is recruiting pilot participants.

stages.title: Full-spectrum sensing
stages.desc: Beyond the boundaries of language. Voice tone, pauses, silence — the things you can't say are often the most authentic data.

stages.title: Embodied companion
stages.desc: A robot with pure visual perception. It's beside you, seeing your expressions, posture, every moment of your life. Your mirror understands you more deeply.

stages.title: Silicon immortality
stages.desc: From the moment you became conscious to the moment your body fails — your silicon life has recorded all of you. Not a copy, but a continuation on a different medium.
